name: Call Bridge
description: Call Bridge (also known as Call Break in South Asia) is a 4-player trick-taking card game enormously popular in Nepal, India, and Bangladesh. It resembles Spades but with individual bidding â€” each player bids the number of tricks they will win, and Spades are permanent trump. Unlike exact-bid games, players must win AT LEAST their bid (over-tricks are allowed but under-tricks are penalised). It is one of the most widely played card games in Nepal.

history.origins: Call Bridge/Call Break is deeply embedded in Nepali card culture and is widely played throughout South Asia. It likely developed from Whist-family games introduced during the British colonial period, merged with local bidding traditions.
timeline: Early-mid 1900s: Spreads across Nepal, India, Bangladesh as a social card game.
Present: The dominant card game in Nepal; played digitally on multiple apps with millions of users.
history.cultural: A staple of Nepali social life. Digital implementations have made it one of the most popular mobile card games in South Asia.
history.evolution: The distinctive 'at least your bid' scoring system (rather than exact-bid) differentiates it from Spades and makes overbidding a viable strategy.

setup.deck: 52 standard cards. Spades are permanent trump.

rules.objective: Score the most points over agreed rounds (usually 5) by winning at least your bid each hand.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal 13 cards each. 2. Each player bids number of tricks they will win (min 1). 3. Player left of dealer leads. 4. Follow suit; must trump if void and holding spades. 5. Spades are permanent trump. 6. Highest card of led suit or trump wins trick. 7. Win at least your bid: +bid; fail: -bid; over-tricks +0.1 each.
keyRules: Spades are ALWAYS trump â€” no other suit can be called.
You MUST trump if you cannot follow suit and hold spades.
Over-tricks count as 0.1 points each (minor bonus).
Under-bidding (failing to make your bid) results in a penalty of -bid.

strategy.basic: Bid conservatively based on your spades (trump) â€” each spade is likely to win a trick. Bid 1 for a weak hand.
strategy.intermediate: Count your high cards carefully: Ace, King, Queen of any suit + all spades. Bid your confident tricks only.
strategy.advanced: Position Awareness: In later bidding positions, you know (partially) what others have bid. If three players bid 8 tricks total, the remaining distribution gives you endgame information. Trump Forcing: Lead low spades to exhaust opponents' trump supply.
tips: Never bid 0 â€” minimum bid is 1.
Over-tricks only earn 0.1 pts each â€” don't chase them at the cost of failing your bid.

variations.name: Call Break (Nepal variant)
variations.description: Most common Nepali form. Identical mechanics. Often played to exactly 5 rounds.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Nepal variant uses same mechanics as base; no engine parameter overrides needed.

scoring.description: Decimal scoring: met bid = bid value + 0.1 per over-trick; failed = -bid.
scoring.winCondition: Highest score after agreed number of rounds (typically 5).

synthesis.shortDescription: South Asia's beloved bid-and-take game. Spades are always trump. Bid how many tricks you'll win â€” hit it or lose that many points. Over 5 rounds, the highest cumulative score wins.
